_comment: RESEARCH-REVIEW backlog — the research/evidence pipeline, NOT trading performance. Split from performance-review-backlog.json 2026-08-30 on the same reasoning as the 2026-05-26 three-way review split: a different RUBRIC wants a different backlog. 'this sweep needs re-running at higher n' and 'this strategy's win rate slipped' are graded against different bars and would bury each other in one file. WHAT BELONGS HERE: a sweep that landed and nobody read; a queue job blocked or underpowered; a harness that produced a number nobody can reproduce; a corpus whose provenance is unclear; an analysis that must be re-run at higher n before it decides anything. WHAT DOES NOT: a strategy tweak (performance), a wiring bug (health), a model promotion (ml). FILE THROUGH scripts/ops/backlog_append.py::append_row, NEVER by hand — it round-trips the exact serialisation and refuses a row restating one already filed.

items.title: 78 landed research units were never read, and the m20 half is largely below its own power floor
items.detail: First run of scripts/research/research_disposition.py --report (2026-08-30) over the two committed corpora: 92 unread / 196 superseded_unread / 0 dispositioned. This session dispositioned the 14 e35 units from RQ-20260830-002, leaving 78 unread, essentially all m20. POPULATION for the power claim: over the newest run per leg, 318 m20 rows carry base_trades_OOS on 317 of them, and 247 sit BELOW the 49.06 floor implied by the queue's own declared power block (n >= (z_a/2 + z_b)^2 / d^2 at alpha=0.05, power=0.80, d=0.4). Observed values run 30-36 with one leg at 4. NOT A BUG IN THE CORPUS - the rows are honest measurements; the finding is that nobody has read them and that most of them cannot answer their own question at the n they hold.
items.why_it_matters: R1-R6 of the research architecture stop at 'landed'; no stage covered 'read', and no review skill referenced the corpora at all (grep returned 0 across all five). So compute was spent, rows were committed, and no decision was ever derived from them. An underpowered unit is worse than an unread one if it is read carelessly: R4's whole point is that an underpowered run manufactures a false finding, and 329 historical honest_negative verdicts already sit at a median OOS base of 33 trades.
items.next_action: In the next /performance-review, work stage 3 of the research-pipeline section: run --unread-only, grade each unit's n_oos against its declared floor FIRST, and disposition it as 'underpowered' (converting to a data-acquisition task) rather than reading a verdict off it. Do not batch-disposition to clear the count - append() refuses a vacuous reason.
items.resolution_criteria: Closes when every unit reported 'unread' by research_disposition.py carries a ledger entry with a non-vacuous reason, AND the units graded 'underpowered' have either an enqueued data-acquisition job or a stated reason why more n is unobtainable. Re-running the report and seeing a lower number is NOT sufficient - a superseding run also lowers it.
items.source: first run of the research-disposition ledger

items.title: The e35 bracket corpus records no OOS sample size, so its rows cannot be power-graded at all
items.area: research pipeline / M40 R1 results contract
items.detail: R1 of docs/research/RESEARCH-WORKFLOW-ARCHITECTURE-2026-08-27.md makes a row inadmissible unless it carries 'its power: n, and the minimum detectable effect'. MEASURED over the whole e35 corpus (n=8,321 rows, 42 distinct keys): the ONLY key resembling a sample size is `split_target_oos`, present on 377 rows (4.5%) and carrying the value 50 - which is the sweep's TARGET, not the achieved out-of-sample trade count. There is no e35 equivalent of m20's `base_trades_OOS`. CONSEQUENCE, observed not predicted: the disposition ledger graded 78 unread units on 2026-08-30 and could power-grade every m20 unit (10 clearing the 49.06 floor, 40 below it) while 27 e35 units were left UNREAD because there is nothing in the row to grade them against. NOT a defect in the measurements themselves - the R-deltas and gate verdicts are honest; the gap is that the row cannot state the denominator its own verdict rests on.
items.why_it_matters: R4 makes the power gate BLOCKING precisely because an underpowered run costs compute AND manufactures a false finding. A corpus that cannot report n cannot be put through that gate, so every e35 verdict is consumed on trust. This is the same shape as the repo's own 'ALWAYS STATE THE POPULATION' rule: a number whose denominator is unavailable is not quotable, and 8,321 such rows are currently the largest research artifact the fleet holds.
items.next_action: Add the achieved OOS trade count to the e35 extractor (scripts/research/e35_corpus_extract.py) so new rows carry it, and decide explicitly whether historical rows are backfillable from the sweep reports or must stay ungradeable. Do NOT back-fill a zero or the target value - that would assert an observation nobody made, which is the fabrication class provenance.py exists to stop.
items.resolution_criteria: Closes when a NEW e35 sweep lands rows carrying an achieved OOS sample size AND research_disposition.py can power-grade them (N_FIELD['e35'] stops being None). Historical rows staying ungradeable is an acceptable outcome IF that is recorded as a deliberate decision rather than left implicit.
items.source: first power-grading pass of the disposition ledger

items.summary: research_queue.observed_n_by_leg keeps the BEST achieved n per leg with no notion of the run configuration that produced it, so a corpus-grounded feasibility check counts observations from a DIFFERENT config as evidence about the one about to run — and on a raise it deadlocks the unit that would produce the new evidence.
items.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-31 while raising e35's `split_target_oos` 50 -> 60 for RQ-20260830-002.

`observed_n_by_leg(corpus)` reduces the corpus to {leg: best n_oos} and `grade_power`'s corpus-grounded branch compares that against the power floor. Nothing in either function knows what run SETTINGS produced an observation, although the corpus rows carry them (`split_target_oos` is a column on every e35 row).

TWO CONSEQUENCES, and the second is the dangerous one:
(1) STALE-CONFIG EVIDENCE. After a raise, pre-raise rows remain the best observation for every leg, so a `source: corpus` check grades the NEW config against the OLD config's achieved n.
(2) DEADLOCK. Measured on the 9 capable legs: pre-raise min_per_leg is 46 against a floor of 49.06, so grounding RQ-20260830-002 on the corpus today returns INFEASIBLE and BLOCKS the dispatch — the only thing that would produce post-raise evidence. Scoping observations by config does not fix it either: with zero matching rows the grade flips INFEASIBLE -> UNVERIFIABLE, which also blocks.

WORKED AROUND, NOT FIXED: the unit is declared `source: none` with an accrual_basis naming the raise and the exact condition under which it becomes corpus-grounded. That is honest (a configuration nothing has ever run genuinely has no corpus-grounded feasibility) but it needs a HUMAN to come back and switch it, and nothing enforces that they do — which is the same 'carried forward in prose' shape as BL-20260825-OPERATOR-OWED-ITEMS-HAVE-NO-REGISTER-NO-AGE-AND-NO-ESCALATION.
items.resolution_criteria: `observed_n_by_leg` accepts a config scope (e.g. feasibility.observed_where: {split_target_oos: 60}) and counts only rows matching it, AND a first-run-under-a-new-config is representable without deadlocking — i.e. the gate can say 'no evidence yet under this configuration' as a RUNNABLE state distinct from both INFEASIBLE (the data refutes it) and UNVERIFIABLE (we could not look). Verified by a test that a raise does not block the unit, and that a pre-raise row does not satisfy a post-raise scope.
